advances: The repaired mass rule with three-site tails is false. The unchanged two-scale family of accepted fact 1484240960b8b9ad satisfies every repaired own-prefix hypothesis, including prefix zero, while its original ratio \(Z_4/Z_3\) tends to infinity. Aligning the adaptive tails with the original three-site mass telescope therefore does not supply a uniform original-mass comparison. This refutes only the repaired auxiliary rule, not the locked weak Oertel conjecture or the earlier binary-tail rule.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The new three-site scalar assertions, the proposed stability interval, and every all-prefix condition were proved by finite sums and exact elementary bounds above.
proof:
Accepted fact 1484240960b8b9ad gives this exact legal family, the unique positive \(\beta\), its bounds \(3/(4M)<\beta<1/M\), the full minimizer \(s_\star\), the active set \(\mathcal J(s_\star)=\lbrace t_0,t_0+1\rbrace\), the bound \(T\ge4M\ell^2\), and (3). Its costs, multiplicities, height weights, cap and tilt are exactly those above. The costs are sorted because \(\ell>10\), and every fourth cost is \(2B_i-1\). We prove every assertion involving the changed three-site tails below.

For one coordinate with cost \(B\), let the scalar subscript \(a=3,4\) specify its alphabet \(\lbrace0,\ldots,a-1\rbrace\). Write its scalar quantities as \(P_{a,B},Z_{a,B},\mu_{a,B},\rho_{a,B},\delta_{a,B}\). The exact alias map is \(\widehat P_i^{(j)}=P_{4,B_i}\) for \(i\le j\) and \(P_{3,B_i}\) otherwise, identically for \(Z,\mu,\rho,\delta\); thus \(\widehat R_i^{(j)}=s^2\rho_{a,B_i}\). These scalar aliases never denote binary-tail prefixes.

Expand a root-kernel cube by an ordered triple \(\mathbf a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)\) of displacements, with tuple energy and radius contribution
$$
\xi=4g(\lambda)+\tfrac43\sum_{q=1}^3e_\lambda(a_q),\qquad
\mathfrak a=g(\lambda)^2+\tfrac13\sum_{q=1}^3[e_\lambda(a_q)^2+b_\lambda(a_q)^2].
\tag{4}
$$
Its weight is \(e^{-s\xi}\) and its normalizer is \(P_{a,B}\). Its root marginal is the prescribed root law; given a root its three slots are independent with the prescribed displacement law. Hence
$$
\mu_{a,B}=\tfrac14\mathbb E_s\xi,\qquad \rho_{a,B}=1+\mathbb E_s\mathfrak a,\qquad
\tfrac14(\log P_{a,B})'=-\mu_{a,B}.
\tag{5}
$$
Here \((\xi,\mathfrak a)\) are exactly \((\Xi,A)\) in the scalar proof of b90bdf64e7944ce3, and \(\rho\) is its extended \(R/s^2\). This is a finite scalar identity and makes no independence claim about an original epigraph law.

For three sites the full tuple list, grouped by the number \(r\) of nonzero slots at root 1, is
$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{root}&\xi&\mathfrak a&\text{multiplicity}\\ \hline
0&0&0&1\\
1&4+\frac23(B-2)r&1+\frac r6(B^2-2B+2)&\binom3r2^r\quad(0\le r\le3)\\
2&4B&B^2&1.
\end{array}
\tag{6}
$$
Both energy and radius contribution are nondecreasing along this list: the root-1 maximum energy is \(2B\), and its maximum radius contribution is \((B^2-2B+4)/2\le B^2\). Thus every tuple pair has \((\mathfrak a-\mathfrak a')(\xi-\xi')\ge0\). The pair of root 0 and root 1 with \(r=0\) makes this product strictly positive. All tuple weights are positive at finite \(s\). Differentiating the finite sums gives
$$
\rho_{3,B}'=-\operatorname{Cov}_s(\mathfrak a,\xi)<0,\qquad
\mu_{3,B}'=-\tfrac14\operatorname{Var}_s(\xi)<0.
\tag{7}
$$
For the first assertion, use the exact pair formula
\(\operatorname{Cov}(\mathfrak a,\xi)=\tfrac12\sum_{u,v}p_up_v(\mathfrak a_u-\mathfrak a_v)(\xi_u-\xi_v)\).
The variance is positive because energies 0 and 4 both occur. The four-site versions of (7) are given by b90bdf64e7944ce3 with its \(C_4=2B-1\) and map (4)-(5). All derivatives include zero by their continuous finite-sum formulas.

It follows that \(\widehat L_j\) and \(\widehat\mu^{(j)}\) are strictly decreasing. The smooth part of \(\widehat\Psi_j\) has strictly increasing derivative \(-\widehat\mu^{(j)}-\widehat L_j\). Since \(\mathcal F\) is convex, every \(\widehat\Psi_j\) is strictly convex on its whole compact domain and has a unique global minimizer. At zero the unique active height is 0 because \(f_t<f_0\) for \(t>0\). Its right derivative is \(-\widehat\mu^{(j)}(0)-\widehat L_j(0)<0\), since \(k>0\). All minimizers are positive.

Adding the fourth site leaves all root-0 and root-1 tuples unchanged. At root 2 it adds 26 tuples of energy \(4B\), with radius contributions \(B^2+(r/3)(B-1)^2\) for their respective slot counts \(r\). It also adds the root-3 tuple, with energy \(8B-4\) and radius contribution \((2B-1)^2\). Every added energy is at least every three-site energy, and every added radius contribution is at least every three-site radius contribution. The three-site distribution has positive mass at zero. Therefore \(\mu_{4,B}>\mu_{3,B}\) and \(\rho_{4,B}\ge\rho_{3,B}\) at every finite rate. Thus
$$
\frac d{ds}(\widehat\Psi_{j+1}-\widehat\Psi_j)
=-(\mu_{4,B_{j+1}}-\mu_{3,B_{j+1}})-(\widehat L_{j+1}-\widehat L_j)<0.
\tag{8}
$$
Decreasing differences order the global minima. Indeed, if \(u>v\) minimized \(\widehat\Psi_j\) and \(\widehat\Psi_{j+1}\), respectively, their minimizing inequalities would give
\((\widehat\Psi_{j+1}-\widehat\Psi_j)(u)-(\widehat\Psi_{j+1}-\widehat\Psi_j)(v)\ge0\), contrary to (8). Hence \(0<\widehat s_0\le\cdots\le\widehat s_k=s_\star\). This is the elementary objective comparison in 30375b78b4633f77 with the functions explicitly replaced by the hatted ones; no binary-tail scalar estimate is imported.

We now prove the lower endpoint in (1). Put \(\theta=Ms_\star\) and \(s_-=(1-1/(10\ell))s_\star\). The elementary logarithm bounds give \(1-1/(2M)\le\theta<1\), \(\theta\ge3/4\), and \(0<s_\star<1/M<1/100\). Throughout \(s\in[s_-,s_\star]\), an expensive coordinate satisfies
$$
v=sB\ge\tfrac34(\ell-1/10)\ge\tfrac23\ell,\qquad q=e^{-2v/3}<1/100.
\tag{9}
$$
For either alphabet, put \(x=e^{-4s/3}\). The exact kernel polynomials are
$$
P_{3,B}=1+(x+2q)^3+q^6,\qquad
P_{4,B}=1+(x+2q)^3+27q^6+e^{4s}q^{12}.
\tag{10}
$$
Here \(x^2=e^{-8s/3}>3/4\), \(e^{4s}<2\), and \(P_{3,B}\le P_{4,B}<4\): the cube is less than 2 and the last two terms in \(P_{4,B}\) are each less than \(1/2\).

In the three-site tuple law, root 0 has probability \(1/P_{3,B}\), while the root-1 tuples with one nonzero slot have total probability \(6x^2q/P_{3,B}\) and energy \(E_1=4+\tfrac23(B-2)\ge2B/3\). The variance pair formula, using only their pairs with root zero, gives
$$
-\mu_{3,B}'(s)=\tfrac14\operatorname{Var}_s(\xi)
\ge\frac{6x^2qE_1^2}{4P_{3,B}^2}\ge\frac{B^2q}{32}.
\tag{11}
$$
For expensive coordinates, \(h e^{-2\ell\theta/3}\ge\ell^2\); since \(s\le s_\star\), their sum of \(q\)'s is at least \(\ell^2\) throughout this interval. All other means are decreasing too. Integrating (11) yields
$$
\widehat\mu^{(0)}(s_-)-\widehat\mu^{(0)}(s_\star)
\ge\frac{M^2\ell^4}{32}\frac{s_\star}{10\ell}
\ge\frac{3M\ell^3}{1280}>\frac{M\ell^2}{4},
\tag{12}
$$
where the last strict inequality uses \(\ell\ge120\).

We bound the fourth-only perturbation at \(s_\star\) separately. Put \(d=e^{-4s_\star B}\). The added root-2 tuples have total weight \(26d\) and radius numerator \([26B^2+18(B-1)^2]d\le44B^2d\): the sum of their nonzero-slot counts is 54. The root-3 tuple has weight \(z=e^{-s_\star(8B-4)}\le d\), mean-energy contribution at most \(2Bz\), and radius contribution at most \(4B^2z\). Since \(P_{4,B}\ge1\), comparison of the normalized mixtures gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
0\le\mu_{4,B}(s_\star)-\mu_{3,B}(s_\star)&\le28B e^{-4s_\star B},\\
0\le\rho_{4,B}(s_\star)-\rho_{3,B}(s_\star)&\le48B^2e^{-4s_\star B}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
$$
For the first upper bound, discard the nonnegative subtraction of the old mean from the added mixture; its added numerator is at most \(26Bd+2Bz\). The radius comparison is identical with the just-computed radius numerators.

Define, only for these estimates, \(D_1=\sum_iB_i e^{-4s_\star B_i}\) and \(D_2=\sum_iB_i^2e^{-4s_\star B_i}\). The bounds \(\theta\ge3/4\) and \(h\le2e^{2\ell/3}\ell^2\) give
$$
\begin{aligned}
D_1&\le M\ell^2[10e^{-30}+2\ell e^{-7\ell/3}]<\frac{M\ell^2}{10000},\\
D_2&\le M^2\ell^2[100e^{-30}+2\ell^2e^{-7\ell/3}]<\frac{M^2\ell^2}{100000}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
$$
These are exact elementary inequalities: \(2\ell^2e^{-\ell/3}<1\) for \(\ell\ge120\), since it decreases there and its value at 120 is less than \(28800/2^{40}<1\). The brackets are therefore bounded by \(10e^{-30}+e^{-240}\) and \(100e^{-30}+e^{-240}\), respectively. Using \(e>2\), these are less than \(11/2^{30}<1/10000\) and \(101/2^{30}<1/100000\).

Summing (13) and using \(\sqrt{u+v}-\sqrt u\le\sqrt v\), we obtain
$$
\begin{aligned}
0\le\mu(s_\star)-\widehat\mu^{(0)}(s_\star)&\le28D_1<\frac{M\ell^2}{100},\\
0\le L(s_\star)-\widehat L_0(s_\star)&\le40\sqrt{48D_2}<M\ell.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
$$
The last inequality uses \(40^2\cdot48=76800<100000\). Since \(1/100+1/120<1/4\), their sum is less than \(M\ell^2/4\). Also \(\widehat L_0(s_-)\ge\widehat L_0(s_\star)\) by (7). With (12), this proves
$$
\widehat\mu^{(0)}(s_-)+\widehat L_0(s_-)>\mu(s_\star)+L(s_\star)\ge t_0.
\tag{16}
$$
Every active height at \(s_-<s_\star\) is at most \(t_0\): comparing two active affine lines at the two rates orders their slopes, and \(t_0\) is active at \(s_\star\). The right derivative of \(\widehat\Psi_0\) at \(s_-\) is therefore at most \(t_0-\widehat\mu^{(0)}(s_-)-\widehat L_0(s_-)<0\). Its unique global minimum lies strictly to the right of \(s_-\). The earlier ordering proves (1) for all prefixes, including zero. Every own minimum is thus globally unique and interior.

We verify high active heights on this whole interval. In fact \(\beta<9/(10M)\). The defining function \(G(y)=M(e^y-1)+e^{-2My}-1\) satisfies
\(G(9/(10M))>9/10+e^{-9/5}-1>9/10+1/9-1>0\), where \(e<3\) gives \(e^{-9/5}>1/9\). Its strict convexity and unique positive zero, proved in 1484240960b8b9ad, imply the bound. Further, \(\theta\ge1-1/(2M)\ge99/100\) and \(1-1/(10\ell)>99/100\), so \(s_->19/(20M)\).

If a height \(t\le T/2\) were active at some \(s\ge s_-\), comparison with its forward neighbor would imply
$$
s\le\log(f_t/f_{t+1})\le\beta+\frac1{T-t}\le\beta+\frac2T
<\frac9{10M}+\frac1{2M\ell^2}<\frac{19}{20M}<s_-.
\tag{17}
$$
Indeed, with \(r=e^{-\beta}\), the exact ratio is
\(f_t/f_{t+1}=e^\beta[1+r^{T-t}/\sum_{q=0}^{T-t-1}r^q]\); its bracket is at most \(1+1/(T-t)\). This is the unchanged height-tail inequality in 30375b78b4633f77, with the same \(T,\beta,f_t\). Here \(t<T\) and the denominator is positive. The strict estimates use \(T\ge4M\ell^2\) and \(\ell^2>10\). Contradiction proves that every active height at every repaired own minimum exceeds \(T/2\).

Finally we prove simultaneous failure of all the own tests. Throughout \(s\in[s_-,s_\star]\), every tuple energy is nonnegative, so \(P_{a,B}(s)\le P_{4,B}(0)=56\), while \(Z_{a,B}(s)\ge1\). Each cheap coordinate has \(\delta_{a,B}(s)\le\log448<7\).

For an expensive coordinate use the scalar comparison polynomials \(P_{\rm bin}=1+e^{-4s}\), \(Z_{\rm bin}=1+e^{-s}\). From (10), \(q<1/100\), and \(e^{4s}<2\),
$$
\begin{aligned}
P_{a,B}-P_{\rm bin}&\le6e^{-8s/3}q+12e^{-4s/3}q^2+8q^3+27q^6+e^{4s}q^{12}\le8q,\\
\delta_{a,B}(s)&\le2s^2+8q.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
$$
For the last assertion use \(Z_{a,B}\ge Z_{\rm bin}\), \(P_{\rm bin}\ge1\), and \(\log(1+u)\le u\). The comparison surplus equals
\(\log[8P_{\rm bin}/Z_{\rm bin}^4]=\log\cosh(2s)-4\log\cosh(s/2)\le2s^2\), by \(\log\cosh x\le x^2/2\). These comparison polynomials do not introduce a binary-tail prefix law.

The common expensive-coordinate \(q=e^{-2s\ell M/3}\) obeys
$$
\ell^2\le hq\le\ell^2\exp\left(\frac{\ell}{3M}+\frac1{15}\right)+1
\le\frac{10}{9}\ell^2+1<2\ell^2.
\tag{19}
$$
The lower bound uses \(s\le s_\star\), \(\theta<1\), and the definition of \(h\). The upper bound uses \(s\ge s_-\), \(1-\theta\le1/(2M)\), \(M\ge10\ell\), and \(e^{1/10}\le10/9\). Since \(2hs^2<2h/M^2<1\), every prefix at every such rate satisfies
$$
\sum_i\widehat\delta_i^{(j)}(s)<7\ell^2+1+16\ell^2\le24\ell^2.
\tag{20}
$$
In either three or four sites, the exact joint probability at root 1 of a nonzero displacement is \(2q(e^{-4s/3}+2q)^2/P_{a,B}\). Its squared factor exceeds \(3/4\), and \(P_{a,B}<16\), so this probability exceeds \(3q/32\). Every such displacement has \(b^2=B^2/4\). An expensive coordinate therefore contributes \(R_{a,B}(s)>3(sB)^2q/128\). Summing, using (9) and (19), gives for every prefix
$$
\widehat V_s^{(j)}>\frac3{128}\left(\frac{2\ell}3\right)^2\ell^2
=\frac{\ell^4}{96}>\frac{\ell^4}{100}.
\tag{21}
$$
Thus \(256\sqrt{\widehat V_s^{(j)}}>(128/5)\ell^2>24\ell^2\). Evaluating (20)-(21) at each own minimum in (1) proves (2) strictly, even without its positive term \(4\widehat s_j\). This includes prefix zero and every intermediate prefix, irrespective of its position in either cost group.

We have verified every repaired hypothesis on one unchanged exact family: legal sorted costs, fixed original multiplicities and weights, the same integer cap and tilt, all unique interior global own minima, all high active heights, and all failed own tests. The unbounded ratio (3) is the original-law assertion of 1484240960b8b9ad under the literal map above. No adaptive partition function has replaced an original mass. This proves the counterexample.
statement:
For every integer \(\ell\ge120\), take exactly the following family from accepted fact 1484240960b8b9ad:
$$
\begin{aligned}
m&=\ell^2,& h&=\left\lceil e^{2\ell/3}\ell^2\right\rceil,& k&=m+h,& M&=2^{20}k^2,\\
B_i&=10M\quad(i\le m),&B_i&=\ell M\quad(i>m),& C_{4,i}&=2B_i-1,&g_i&=(0,1,B_i,2B_i-1),\\
s_\star&=\log(1+1/M),&M(e^\beta-1)&=1-e^{-2M\beta},&\beta&>0.
\end{aligned}
$$
All spatial sites have unit multiplicity, and every feasible original atom \((\mathbf x,t)\) has weight \(e^{-\beta t}\). Define the full four-site scalar quantities \(\mu(s),V_s,L(s)\) exactly as in 1484240960b8b9ad and retain its same cap
\(t_0=\lfloor\mu(s_\star)+L(s_\star)\rfloor\), \(T=t_0+2M\).
The cap is not recomputed using a restricted alphabet.

Here are the repaired quantities, distinguished from the accepted binary-tail prefix objects of 30375b78b4633f77. For \(0\le j\le k\), put \(\widehat D_i^{(j)}=\lbrace0,1,2,3\rbrace\) if \(i\le j\), and \(\widehat D_i^{(j)}=\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace\) otherwise. For every allowed root \(\lambda\), define
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat I_{i,\lambda}^{(j)}&=\lbrace a\in\mathbb Z:\lambda+a,\lambda-a\in\widehat D_i^{(j)}\rbrace,\\
e_{i,\lambda}(a)&=\tfrac12[g_i(\lambda+a)+g_i(\lambda-a)]-g_i(\lambda),\\
b_{i,\lambda}(a)&=\tfrac12[g_i(\lambda+a)-g_i(\lambda-a)],\\
\widehat K_{s,i}^{(j)}(\lambda)&=\sum_{a\in\widehat I_{i,\lambda}^{(j)}}e^{-(2s/3)[g_i(\lambda+a)+g_i(\lambda-a)]},\\
\widehat H_{s,i}^{(j)}(\lambda)&=\sum_{a\in\widehat I_{i,\lambda}^{(j)}}e^{-(4s/3)e_{i,\lambda}(a)},\\
\widehat P_i^{(j)}(s)&=\sum_{\lambda\in\widehat D_i^{(j)}}\widehat K_{s,i}^{(j)}(\lambda)^3,\\
\widehat Z_i^{(j)}(s)&=\sum_{x\in\widehat D_i^{(j)}}e^{-sg_i(x)},\qquad
\widehat\delta_i^{(j)}(s)=\log\frac{8\widehat P_i^{(j)}(s)}{\widehat Z_i^{(j)}(s)^4}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Let \(\widehat J_i\) have probabilities \(\widehat K_{s,i}^{(j)}(\lambda)^3/\widehat P_i^{(j)}(s)\). Given this root, let \(\widehat V_i\) have probabilities \(e^{-(4s/3)e_{i,\lambda}(a)}/\widehat H_{s,i}^{(j)}(\lambda)\). The displacement variable \(\widehat V_i\) is distinct from the total radius \(\widehat V_s^{(j)}\). Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\mu_i^{(j)}(s)&=\mathbb E[g_i(\widehat J_i)+e_{i,\widehat J_i}(\widehat V_i)],\\
\widehat\rho_i^{(j)}(s)&=1+\mathbb E[g_i(\widehat J_i)^2+e_{i,\widehat J_i}(\widehat V_i)^2+b_{i,\widehat J_i}(\widehat V_i)^2],\\
\widehat R_i^{(j)}(s)&=s^2\widehat\rho_i^{(j)}(s),\qquad \widehat V_s^{(j)}=\sum_i\widehat R_i^{(j)}(s),\\
\widehat\mu^{(j)}(s)&=\sum_i\widehat\mu_i^{(j)}(s),\qquad
\widehat L_j(s)=40\sqrt{\sum_i\widehat\rho_i^{(j)}(s)}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The finite expectations define \(\widehat\rho\) and \(\widehat L\) at zero as well. The squared imbalance has exactly the convention of 30375b78b4633f77.

Retain the same height quantities for every alphabet:
$$
\begin{aligned}
f_E&=\sum_{t=E}^T e^{-\beta t}\quad(0\le E\le T),\qquad f_E=0\quad(E>T),\\
\mathcal F(s)&=\max_{0\le t\le T,\ t\in\mathbb Z}[\log(f_t/f_0)+st],\\
\mathcal J(s)&=\lbrace t:\log(f_t/f_0)+st=\mathcal F(s)\rbrace,\\
\widehat\Psi_j(s)&=\mathcal F(s)+\tfrac14\sum_i\log\widehat P_i^{(j)}(s)-\int_0^s\widehat L_j(y)\,dy,
\quad 0\le s\le s_{\max}=12\log2.
\end{aligned}
$$
The unchanged height quantities need no new prefix superscript. The unadorned full scalar quantities \(P_i,Z_i,\mu_i,R_i,V_s,L\) of 1484240960b8b9ad equal the hatted quantities at \(j=k\), and its \(\Psi\) equals \(\widehat\Psi_k\). For \(j<k\), these are not the binary-tail objects \(D_i^{(j)},P_i^{(j)},\Psi_j\) of 30375b78b4633f77: only the formulas are retained, while the tail alphabets change. The local excess and imbalance formulas agree whenever their endpoints are allowed.

Every \(\widehat\Psi_j\), including \(j=0\), has a unique global minimizer \(\widehat s_j\), and
$$
\left(1-\frac1{10\ell}\right)s_\star<\widehat s_0\le\widehat s_1\le\cdots\le\widehat s_k=s_\star<s_{\max}.
\tag{1}
$$
For every \(0\le j\le k\), all heights in \(\mathcal J(\widehat s_j)\) exceed \(T/2\), and its own test fails:
$$
\sum_i\widehat\delta_i^{(j)}(\widehat s_j)<256\sqrt{\widehat V_{\widehat s_j}^{(j)}}+4\widehat s_j.
\tag{2}
$$
Nevertheless, the complete original epigraph masses
\(\Gamma(\mathbf x)=\sum_i g_i(x_i)\) and
\(Z_a=\sum_{\mathbf x\in\lbrace0,\ldots,a-1\rbrace^k}f_{\Gamma(\mathbf x)}\), for \(a=3,4\), satisfy
$$
\frac{Z_4}{Z_3}\ge\frac14\left(1+\frac{e^{-20}}3\right)^{\ell^2}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{3}
$$
The locked \(n,d,C,\Lambda,S,W,c_0\), and arithmetic \(N\) retain their original meanings.
